concept.name: Commission
concept.definition: The fee a broker charges a customer for executing a trade, historically per trade or per share/contract. Commissions are the visible, contractual component of trading cost and are disclosed on confirmations; many retail equity brokers have moved to zero commission, monetizing order flow instead.
concept.intuition: The commission is the broker's sticker price for doing the trade - the one cost line everyone sees before the market takes its invisible share.
concept.mechanics: Charged as a flat ticket charge, per share/contract, or as a percentage of principal; Rule 10b-10 requires written disclosure at or before completion of the transaction of the remuneration the broker received from the customer. Zero-commission models substitute payment for order flow and other revenue, shifting rather than eliminating cost.
concept.formula: Total commission = per-unit rate x quantity (or flat ticket charge), per the brokerage agreement.
concept.failure_modes: Per-trade commissions penalize small and frequent orders disproportionately, distorting strategy design; conversely, zero-commission pricing obscures the real cost structure and encourages overtrading. Per-share schedules with minimums can also exceed the expected value of tiny trades.
concept.misconceptions: Zero commission is not zero cost - spread, impact, exchange/clearing fees, and order-flow economics remain. Nor is the commission the biggest cost for size: implicit costs dominate institutional trading.
concept.example: A broker charging $0.005 per share bills $5.00 on a 1,000-share order; the confirm discloses this remuneration alongside any fees, separate from whatever the venue charged.
